analysis.title: US TMT quick hits: temperature check (Callahan, 23 Nov 2026)
key_insights: NDX rose roughly 715 bps (>5%) on the session, with NVDA adding about $940 bn of market cap in one day, tied to Jensen's reinstatement at Nvidia per the note.
Single-day NDX gains above 5% have historically occurred at or near local lows: April 2025 (Liberation Day lows), Nov 2022 (cool CPI), Mar 2020 (COVID bottoming), Dec 2018 (post-hiking lows).
Durability is debated. NDX is still down about 140 bps on a 3-day basis and up only 70 bps on a 2-day basis.

Desk flows were lighter than expected despite NDX constituent volumes up about 60%. ETF volumes were in the high-30s % of the tape for much of the morning, near YTD highs, possibly reflecting index-level exposure management.
Bulls cite a 'nobody left to sell' positioning tailwind and argue this was a sentiment bear market in AI/semis, not a fundamental one.
Bears cite open questions on China, shell/permitting, ROIs and token trajectory, and expect it to be hard to rally much above pre-Election levels, let alone back to the 200-dma.
Focus shifts to earnings this week (DELL, HPE, ADI), which bulls think could carry a 'glass half full' tone. WDAY is also cited as an earnings set-up.
The close today and the open tomorrow may set the tone for a quieter next 2.5 trading days. NDX remains about 5% below its 200-dma.
Only 3 SOX names (LSCC, MPWR, COHR) are up month-to-date in November, so bulls argue little of the recent pullback has been recovered.
NDX has been in a down-trend since early October. Watch for a break above the trend line and a recovery of the 200-dma.
Client inbound centered on whether the move is real (rally or fade), ZS/CRWD, shopping lists, and internet price action where BKNG, SPOT, UBER and TTWO lag DASH, APP and RBLX.
